soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1: M=∅ sanity reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed extensional reduction to CTFID fails: CTFID decides graph/menu functional identifiability, whereas IDcrit(Q;p) is a pointwise fiber-constancy predicate that can hold at exceptional p even when CTFID correctly returns FAIL.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1: MCTFID and Cfail interfaces
soundness_flags.one_line: MCTFID and Cfail take no p, yet the claimed F and countermodels must be selected for the particular fiber at p and must reproduce its specific menu laws.

soundness_flags.one_line: Formula-denominator and root-derivative margins do not ensure differentiability of sign-conditioned branches; at a branch boundary ∇F and the stated ordinary Wald limit need not exist.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Choose one estimand semantics: either redefine the kernel as universal graph/menu functional identification and retain the CTFID reduction, or make p an explicit input and drop that reduction in favor of a pointwise semialgebraic decision result.
Give Cfail the data needed to compile its witness—at least (G,M,Z,Q,p,trace)—and state whether failure certifies nonidentification at that p or only a global graphical obstruction.

For inference, restrict successful outputs to a locally fixed analytic branch or add explicit positive margins for every branch guard; otherwise formulate a directional-limit and nonstandard confidence procedure.

recommended_next_step: Return to Stage -1: repair the global-versus-pointwise identification semantics and the p-free failure compiler before re-submitting the otherwise genuinely open signed-completeness kernel.
